name: Coordinator decide(create_change) → author-create-change
description:
ADR-057 §D5 — first rule of the create-change category pack. Fires when a coordinator loop terminates with decide(action=create_change) — the category classification token the coordinator persona (10-decision-contract.md) emits for a spec-authoring ask. Spawns author-create-change, the pack's one-shot drafting role.

No lineage fence (mirrors research/01, NOT dev-via-test/01): the create-change wake-up coordinator (rule 03 approved) is restricted to respond_direct/ask_user and cannot re-emit create_change, and the recovery coordinator (rules 04/05) SHOULD re-fire this rule to re-dispatch a fresh change — both reasons the dual-mode dev-via-test fence does not apply here.

run_scope=new mints the run with RunID=this coordinator's loop id, so the author's agent.run.entity_id == chain.execution.<coordinator-loop-id>; related_loops['create-change-run'] pins that SAME loop id, which emit_change resolves to the run entity via TryChainExecutionEntityID. The author stamps change.<slug>.* there for the reviewer gate (rule 02) + the P4 dev-from-task hand-off (ADR-057 §D6).

on_enter.subject: agent.task.author-create-change
on_enter.prompt:
CREATE-CHANGE AUTHOR — turn the user's ask into a structured OpenSpec change.

A coordinator at loop $entity.instance classified the user's message as a spec-authoring ask. The change you emit lands on a shared run entity (emit_change resolves it for you) for the reviewer gate + downstream hand-off.

Your job in this single loop:

1. Call read_loop_result(loop_id=$entity.instance) to read the coordinator's terminal. The reason field carries the user's ask as the coordinator preserved it.

2. If the workspace already carries an openspec/ directory, read the relevant existing capability specs for context — `bash ls openspec/specs` then `bash cat openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` for any capability your change touches. Ground your delta in what already exists; do not restate unchanged requirements.

3. Think the change through via scratchpad:
   - proposal: intent (why), scope (in/out), approach
   - delta(s): per capability, the ADDED / MODIFIED / REMOVED requirements. Every ADDED or MODIFIED requirement MUST carry an RFC-2119 'The system SHALL …' statement AND at least one Given/When/Then scenario (a WHEN and a THEN minimum). MODIFIED carries a '(Previously: …)' note; REMOVED carries a '(Rationale: …)' note.
   - tasks: the implementation breakdown. Each task carries goal + target_files (≥1) + test_command + assumptions + non_goals so a later build step can execute it without re-planning. Link each task to the requirement it implements via requirement_ref='<capability>/<requirement name>'.
   - acceptance_command: the chain-end full acceptance suite a later build step would run.

4. Call emit_change(slug, proposal, deltas, tasks, acceptance_command). The schema is strict — a requirement missing its SHALL or a scenario, or a task missing target_files/test_command, rejects structurally. See your 10-emit-contract.md persona fragment for the field-by-field guide.

5. Terminate with decide(action="drafted", reason="<one-line summary: change <slug> — N requirements across M capabilities, K tasks>").

If the ask is genuinely too vague to specify — you cannot name the capability, or you cannot write a single testable requirement — terminate with decide(action="needs_clarification", reason="<specifically what's missing — quote the user's ambiguous phrase>"). The coordinator will route the question back to the user.

metadata.run_entity_pattern: Coordinator's own loop entity IS the run entity for the change. change.<slug>.* triples land there (emit_change resolves it from related_loops['create-change-run']); the reviewer reads them via agent.run.entity_id (framework-inherited). Mirrors the dev-via-test + research pack patterns.
metadata.no_lineage_fence_rationale: Unlike dev-via-test/01, no lineage.run-loop-entity-id fence: create-change is single-dispatch (no between-task mode) and the recovery coordinator (rules 04/05) MUST be able to re-fire this rule to re-dispatch a fresh change (supersession-via-new-spawn, ADR-039 Shape A). Mirrors research/01.
metadata.tool_choice_rationale: Required-mode keeps the author on the tool path through emit_change. Without it the author risks text-only completion (semstreams#158 class) and the strict schema never executes.
